title: Review of Safe Management Measures with Stability after COVID-19 Omicron Virus Wave
what_it_is: Review of Safe Management Measures with Stability after COVID-19 Omicron Virus Wave

sections.label: COVID-19 safe management measures review
sections.summary: MPs asked the Health Minister whether safe management measures, SafeEntry and one-metre dining distance rules will be reviewed after the Omicron wave peaked.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health given that the COVID-19 Omicron variant virus wave has passed its peak (a) whether the Government will review the overall safe management measures; (b) whether the SafeEntry measure still serve its purpose; and (c) whether the one-metre distance requirement at eating places can be relaxed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health (a) what is the overall cost to businesses to maintain Vaccination-Differentiated Safe Management Measures just to cater to unvaccinated residents; and (b) whether requiring unvaccinated residents to bear their own medical costs will be sufficient deterrence to residents who choose not to be vaccinated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As the Member is aware, the relaxed rules came into effect on 29 March 2022, which is why we are all seated together today, and we have also transitioned to a Vaccinated Travel Framework on 1 April 2022.

sections.label: Unvaccinated share of ICU cases
sections.summary: About 3.5% of adults are not fully vaccinated and account for over one-fifth of ICU cases or deaths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As of now, we have about 3.5% of our adult population that is not fully vaccinated and they account for over one-fifth of cases that require ICU care or die.

sections.label: Keeping vaccination-differentiated measures
sections.summary: The Minister says keeping VDS is the more cautious and correct course to avoid more non-fully vaccinated patients needing hospital care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The more cautious and correct course of action now is to keep VDS and not to risk having more non-fully vaccinated patients getting infected and needing hospital care and adding workload to our healthcare workers.

sections.label: Pandemic crisis not over
sections.summary: Despite eased measures and reopened borders, the pandemic crisis is not over and the situation must continue to be monitored.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, while we have eased up the SMMs and reopened our borders, the pandemic crisis is not over.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We will have to continue to monitor the local and global situation, do our part to keep our country safe and continue to work together to tackle whatever challenges that may come our way.

sections.label: Considering removing VDS later
sections.summary: The Minister says VDS removal can be considered after hospitals are in a better position and healthcare workers have a breather.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Let us go through it a bit more, make sure our hospitals are in a better position, healthcare workers have a breather.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Then, I think we consider whether we can remove the VDS.

sections.label: Vaccination rate unlikely to rise
sections.summary: The Minister says the vaccinated number is unlikely to go up further, with Singapore at 97%, probably the highest in the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But the Member is right that the vaccinated number is unlikely to go up further.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We are at 97% – probably, the highest in the world.

sections.label: Unpredictable virus and judgement calls
sections.summary: The virus is unpredictable, so instead of tying hands, all factors like hospital situation, cases, severe cases and vaccination rate are considered for a judgement call.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Because the virus has, over and over again, proven that it is totally unpredictable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, we would really rather not tie our hands that way but we always look at the entire situation, look into all the unforeseen circumstances, look at the hospital situation, cases, severe cases, vaccination rate, take everything into consideration and make a judgement call.
